$comment: INDOX's VIEWS — layer 2 of the column model: WHERE a column appears, never what it means.
display.json says what a column IS (its Hebrew label, its logical type, its value domain).
This file says where it SHOWS: which columns a screen opens with, in what order, how wide,
and how the rows are sorted. Splitting the two is what lets one table carry more than one
reading of itself — a triage view and an audit view over the same 126 columns — which is
impossible while 'visible' is a property of the column rather than of the view.
GLOBAL, like the catalog. An instance is a tenant of the same product, not a different
product, so a view is authored once and every tenant gets it.
THE URL IS THE OTHER HALF. What is here are the SHIPPED DEFAULTS; an operator's own
deviation — a hidden column, a resize, a different sort — lives in the address bar, which is
already this console's contract ('the view lives in the URL'). That is deliberate: it is
shareable, it restores an exact screen, and it needs no per-user table, no migration and no
server state. The named view is where you start; the URL is where you are.
A column NOT listed in a view still exists — it is simply not on screen, and the column
picker offers it. Never delete a column from the catalog to hide it.
